_about: Kinds every project has (docs/library.md): a project's own kinds in presets/<project>.json add to these and replace one of the same name. docs/3d-characters.md has how a 3D character is made, slot by slot. One full recipe is also the preset shared/character3d.

character3d.description: A 3D character for a game: concept → A-pose → cutout → view sheet (true front, back, left and right of the same character, checked by Claude, never one view) → textured mesh from the sheet (mesh.views3d, best-of-3) → clean+bake → humanoid rig (or robot template) → clips → FBX/GLB and previews. Set data.form to "robot" and data.template (spider|quadarm|biped|chain) for hard-surface creatures. data.unityProject names the Unity folder for the Humanoid check. data.triangles is the clean budget (default 25000).

concept.description: A full-body reference to model from (upload one, or generate a turnaround).

params.prompt: Character turnaround sheet of {name}, {look}: front, side and back views, full body, neutral A-pose, plain light grey background, even light. {style} {feedback}

apose.description: Front view alone: whole body in an A-pose, arms 45° down, legs apart, plain background. What the mesh is made from.

params.prompt: same character, A-pose, arms 45 degrees down, legs apart, front view, plain background. Image 1 is {name}. Keep the exact same design, colors and proportions. Full body from head to feet, facing the viewer, nothing else in the picture. {feedback}

cutout.description: The A-pose with the background removed (transparent PNG).

sheet.description: The view sheet: front, back, left and right of the SAME character side by side on flat grey (1024 px cells), each cut out, checked by Claude for one consistent character before any 3D GPU time is spent. The mesh is made from this, never from one picture. data.form robot (or any non-humanoid) keeps every limb separated and visible in the views; data.look helps the check.

angles.description: Optional extras: close-up, wide, aerial, low-angle and 45°/90° looks at the same character from the cutout (image.angles has no back view). Not used for the mesh: the sheet is.

mesh.description: Textured mesh from the four-view sheet (mesh.views3d, best of 3, judged from 4-angle Blender stills against the concept), then cleaned to the triangle budget and baked. Never from a single image (one view guesses the back).

make.pick: Matches the concept from every angle: correct proportions and silhouette, on-model with the reference, no shards or spikes, texture reads the character, usable as a game mesh.

rig.description: Humanoid: Mixamo-named skeleton via mesh.rig. Robot (data.form=robot): split + template + procedural clips via blender.character. Clips retarget onto this.

motion/*.description: A clip generated from a text prompt on the rig (data.prompt is the sentence). The GLB is this slot; the preview video is preview/{part}. Prefer a Quaternius animation/* when a library move already fits.

animation/*.description: One clip on the rig (library motion:ual1/Walk_Loop, asset:, or slot:). Procedural robot clips come from remaking the rig with form=robot.

preview/turntable.description: A video of the rig. mesh.rig files its walk video here. Making this slot on its own renders a turntable of the rest pose.

preview/*.description: A video of one clip (preview/walk shows animation/walk).

export/fbx.description: The FBX Unity imports: Mixamo bone names (Humanoid-ready), each clip a named take, 1 unit = 1 m. Make it with inputs.files = ["slot:./rig", "slot:./animation/walk", ...] to take those clips along.

export/glb.description: The GLB the web games load: one animation per clip. Make it with inputs.files = ["slot:./rig", "slot:./animation/walk", ...] to take those clips along.

check/humanoid.description: Unity EditMode check: imports export/fbx as Humanoid and asserts avatar.isValid, isHuman, and no missing required bones. Needs data.unityProject (folder under C:\Projects that has com.hawkes.gen). Returns the NUnit totals.
